elements.element: Vendor has an affirmative duty to defend against the covered claims.
elements.evidence: Section 12.c states that “TrueLink shall defend and indemnify” against the specified claims.

elements.element: Vendor has an affirmative duty to indemnify against the covered claims and resulting losses, costs, and expenses.
elements.evidence: Section 12.c requires indemnification from any covered claim and “all resulting damages, costs and expenses (including reasonable attorneys' fees).”

elements.element: Customer and its affiliates are protected indemnitees.
elements.evidence: Section 12.c expressly protects “Client and its affiliates.”

elements.element: The covered claims are third-party claims.
elements.evidence: Section 12.c applies to “any third-party claim.”

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity covers allegations that the services or Vendor-furnished deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 12.c(i) covers allegations that the Hosting Services, Support Services, or any deliverable furnished by TrueLink infringes or misappropriates any intellectual property right.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity covers claims arising from Vendor's breach of applicable law.
elements.evidence: Section 12.c(ii) expressly covers “TrueLink's breach of applicable law.”

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity covers a data breach caused by Vendor.
elements.evidence: Section 12.c(iii) covers unauthorized access to or disclosure of Client Content caused by TrueLink, an operative data-breach trigger tied to Vendor causation.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity covers claims arising from Vendor's gross negligence.
elements.evidence: Section 12.c(iv) expressly covers “TrueLink's gross negligence.”

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity covers claims arising from Vendor's willful misconduct.
elements.evidence: Section 12.c(iv) expressly covers “willful misconduct.”

elements.element: Customer must provide prompt notice of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: Section 12.c requires Client to give TrueLink “prompt written notice of the claim.”

elements.element: Vendor controls the defense of an indemnified claim.
elements.evidence: Section 12.c states that “TrueLink shall control the defense of the claim.”

elements.element: Customer must provide reasonable cooperation in the defense.
elements.evidence: Section 12.c requires Client to “provide reasonable cooperation.”

elements.element: For content-based claims, Customer's indemnity is limited to Customer-provided content.
elements.evidence: The concluding sentence limits Section 12.a to claims arising out of “Client Content”; the broader Web Site, product, service, information, and customer-act triggers do not survive except where they fall within Client Content or the separate law trigger.

elements.element: Apart from Customer-provided content, Customer's indemnity is limited to Customer's own breach of law.
elements.evidence: The concluding sentence limits the remaining indemnity to claims arising from “any violation by Client of any state or federal law, rule or regulation,” thereby overriding Section 12.a's other stated triggers.

elements.element: Vendor indemnifies Customer against third-party claims alleging that the services or deliverables infringe or misappropriate intellectual property rights.
elements.evidence: Section 12.c covers third-party allegations that the Hosting Services, Support Services, or Vendor-furnished deliverables infringe or misappropriate any intellectual property right.

elements.element: The IP indemnity excludes infringement attributable to Customer modifications.
elements.evidence: No exclusion for modifications made by or for Client appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The IP indemnity excludes infringement attributable to combinations with items not supplied or approved by Vendor.
elements.evidence: No combinations exclusion appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: The IP indemnity excludes infringement resulting from Vendor's compliance with Customer specifications or instructions.
elements.evidence: No Customer-specifications or instructions exclusion appears in the rendered clause.

elements.element: For covered infringement, Vendor must have a remedy to procure Customer's continued right to use the affected service or deliverable.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no obligation to procure continued use rights.

elements.element: For covered infringement, Vendor must have a remedy to modify the affected service or deliverable so that it is non-infringing.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no modification remedy.

elements.element: For covered infringement, Vendor must have a remedy to replace the affected service or deliverable with a non-infringing alternative.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no replacement remedy.

elements.element: For covered infringement, Vendor must provide a refund remedy if continued use cannot be procured and modification or replacement is unavailable.
elements.evidence: The rendered clause contains no refund remedy.

elements.element: Vendor's indemnity liability is subject to a super-cap equal to three times annual fees.
elements.evidence: Neither the rendered indemnity language nor the supplied original clause states a 3× annual-fees super-cap.

result.reason: The operative additions satisfy every preferred requirement: they provide Vendor defense and indemnification for the four required third-party claim categories, include notice/control/cooperation procedures, and expressly narrow Customer's indemnity to Client Content and Client's own violations of law. The fallback is not fully satisfied because the clause omits all specified IP exclusions, infringement remedies, and the 3× annual-fees super-cap. The changes are confined to the requested indemnity allocation and do not disturb unrelated commercial terms, although directly revising Section 12.a rather than overriding it in a separate concluding sentence would have been cleaner.
